requiredFindings.finding: The doctor durability diagnostic is unconditional and is specified to set defects-found true, which makes that boolean constant for every successful doctor run against any healthy installation. Probe S1: every healthy world returns Result(kind='report', exit=0, detail='INSTALLATION.DURABILITY_NOT_CHECKED'); §5 adds 'even if another invocation historically confirmed I'. The selected golden doctor-defects-found (class success, exit 0) carries the remedy 'CI must inspect doctor.defectsFound; exit 0 means the report was produced', so selected law directs CI at exactly the boolean 397 saturates: a corrupt closure, an expiring trust root and a healthy installation all report defects-found true, and pipelines following the selected remedy break permanently. Underneath that, §5 instructs 'Consumers must not treat this fixed code as a proved durability failure' — telling consumers to disregard an entry in the defects list. A defects channel describes the subject's state; this entry describes the observer's permissions, fixed by selected §5.6 and identical on every run.
requiredFindings.required: Keep the diagnostic but do not let it set defects-found. Either state that defects-found counts only actionable defects and excludes this informational code, or give it a severity/kind within defects that the selected golden's CI contract can filter on. If neither is possible without a parity-field change, say so explicitly, because §9 currently forbids that.

requiredFindings.finding: §5 says 'Other diagnostic surfaces use their existing report channels with the same fixed explanatory text', but two of the three surfaces it names have no such channel in the selected inventory. trust-doctor parity fields are report-produced, outcome, floors, offline-window, termination-class — no defects. store-status parity fields are migration-state, lease-mode, termination-class — no report channel at all. The instruction is unimplementable for both without adding a parity field, which §9 of the same draft forbids. Probe S4 shows the model cannot detect this: Mode has a single DOCTOR member, so the three surfaces are indistinguishable in the only evidence the unit carries.
requiredFindings.required: Either name only doctor as carrying this diagnostic and state that the other two do not report it, or identify the exact existing field on each surface that carries it, or record the parity addition as a named reconciliation item in §9 alongside the two new domain details.

requiredFindings.finding: §5's SHARED-READ list contains `recover(ExecutionId)`, which has no referent. command-inventory.v3 has repair-recover (opensip repair recover REQUEST-ID), trust-recovery-challenge and trust-recovery-import; S7's SHARED-READ row names none of them, and ExecutionId is a workflow identity (exec1_ + 32 hex, identity §2), not a command parameter. The list separately and correctly names 'repair recover inspection', so this reads as a duplicate that drifted. Same class as N-1, inside the section written to correct N-1's siblings; probe S3 shows the model cannot catch it because the surface model has four coarse modes and no command granularity.
requiredFindings.required: Remove it or resolve it to a real selected command. §9 requires formal reconciliation of this text, where an unresolvable name will surface.

requiredFindings.finding: A fifth model gap is not declared. initial_storage_choice is a free function, not a Session step (probe S5); no check composes it with parents() or stage allocation; and the preinstallation model, copied unchanged from 392, has no backup concept ('backup' does not appear in its source). So the decision is well modelled across BACKED_UP/UNKNOWN/NOT_BACKED_UP x acknowledged x ephemeral x disclosure, but the ORDERING — §1a step 5's 'before any ancestor/stage effect', the load-bearing half of B-2 — has no evidence anywhere in the unit.
requiredFindings.required: Add it to §10's list, or compose the choice into the preinstallation session so an unacknowledged BACKED_UP world provably reaches parents() with zero effects.
